title: THE WAITING OF LAST MEETING
summary: A story of love, memories, separation and an unfinished wait.
body:
**Chapter 3 — The Conversations That Slowly Brought Us Closer**



I still remember that evening when I returned from work with a terrible headache. After telling her about the pain, she asked me to come to her room and offered to help me. I accepted her invitation and slowly walked towards her room. I sat beside her, still feeling the heaviness in my head. She gently applied some oil and began taking care of me. There was something very peaceful about that moment. Her calm nature and the gentle way she looked after me made the evening feel different from an ordinary day. I never thought that such a simple moment would become one of the memories I would remember so clearly in the years to come.



While she was taking care of me, we continued talking. Our conversation wasn't about love or anything particularly romantic. We were still in the early stages of knowing each other, and there were so many things we didn't know about one another. We talked about her studies, her preparation and the entrance examination she needed to clear to get admission to a law college. I asked her how much she had studied, which subjects she was preparing for and how things were going. She shared little updates about her preparation, and I listened. Somewhere in my mind, I still wanted to see her succeed in the examination and achieve the reason she had come there.



As our conversation continued, we slowly moved towards other topics. We started sharing information about our families, our parents and our everyday lives. I asked her about her mother, what she did and how things were at home. We also talked about her father, her family background and how many brothers and sisters she had. She shared some details about her family, and I shared a little about mine too. These weren't extraordinary conversations, but they helped us understand each other better. Every conversation revealed something new, and slowly, the distance between two people who had once been strangers started becoming smaller.



Those conversations didn't end with that evening. As the days passed, we started talking more often. Sometimes we discussed studies, sometimes family matters, and sometimes completely different things. We talked about our friends, our villages and the people around us. She also told me about one of her good friends named Sila. I gradually came to know about the people who were part of her life. We also had conversations about her mother, and I found her mother to be a very nice person through the interactions we shared. It felt natural to learn about the people who mattered to her.



By then, almost three or four months had passed since our conversations had started. Without making any special plans, we had begun spending more and more time talking to each other. When I say spending time, I don't mean that we were always sitting together. Much of that time was spent over phone calls. Our conversations became longer and more frequent. We started discussing different things, sharing our daily experiences and telling each other about what was happening in our lives. Sometimes, one topic would lead to another, and before we realised it, quite some time had passed.



After returning from work, I would sometimes call her and ask simple questions. What are you doing? Have you eaten? How was your day? What are you studying now? These were ordinary questions, but they slowly became part of our routine. Sometimes we spoke for five minutes, sometimes ten minutes, and occasionally even longer. We also started having video calls from time to time. Slowly, these small conversations became something I looked forward to after finishing my work. There was no particular reason to call every time. Sometimes, we simply wanted to know what the other person was doing.



Looking back, I realise that those months were filled with so many little conversations. We were discovering each other's personalities, families, friendships and backgrounds. I was learning about her life, and she was learning about mine. We didn't need to discuss anything extraordinary every day. Even the simplest topics could keep our conversations going. I never imagined that these ordinary phone calls would eventually become such an important part of my memories. At that time, everything was moving naturally, one conversation after another, without either of us knowing what the future had in store.



But somewhere between those conversations about friends, villages and family, I came across a family story that I hadn't known before. It was connected to her father, his second marriage and a daughter from that relationship. I listened as these details slowly became part of our conversations. I didn't know the complete story, and I hadn't imagined that there was another side to the family history I was gradually discovering.

But one question remained in my mind: What was the real story behind her father's second marriage, and what would I discover as I learned more about her family?
